part2.intro: Three young people talk about a place in their town that they often visit.
part2.question: For each question, choose the correct answer.

texts.label: A
texts.title: Lucas
texts.text: I go to the sports centre near my school three times a week. I swim in the pool on Mondays and play basketball with my team on Wednesdays and Fridays. It isn't cheap, but my parents pay for it because they think sport is important. The best thing is the café – after training we always sit there together and have a hot chocolate. My coach says I could play for the city team next year.

texts.label: B
texts.title: Mai
texts.text: Our town library is in a beautiful old building next to the post office. I go there every Saturday morning with my little brother. He chooses picture books and I look for detective stories. Everything is free, which is great because books are expensive. Last summer I helped the librarians with a reading club for young children. It was my first job, and I loved it!

texts.label: C
texts.title: Priya
texts.text: When I was younger, I didn't like museums – I thought they were boring. Then my uncle took me to the science museum in the city centre and I changed my mind. There are lots of things you can touch and try. Now I go there with my friends in the school holidays. Students get in for half price. I'd like to work there when I'm older, maybe as a guide.

items.q: Who usually goes to the place with a younger member of their family?
Who says their opinion of the place is different now?
Whose parents pay for them to go to the place?
Who has done some work at the place?
Who meets friends for a drink after doing a sport?
Who pays less to go in because they are at school?
Who hopes to be chosen for something in the future?

part3.title: Summer helper at the tourist office
part3.text:
Every summer, thousands of visitors come to the small seaside town of Porthwell. And this year, many of them got help from fifteen-year-old Nina Clarke.

Nina spent six weeks as a volunteer at the town's tourist information centre. "My aunt works there, and she told me they needed someone who could speak French," says Nina. "My mum is from France, so I speak French at home. I was nervous on the first day, but everyone was very friendly."

Nina answered all kinds of questions. "People wanted to know where the best restaurants were, what time the museum opened, or how to get to the hospital. One man even asked me to find a dentist because he had terrible toothache!" She also helped visitors to book hotel rooms and boat trips.

The hardest part was the phone. "On the phone you can't see people's faces, so it's more difficult to understand them," she explains. "Some callers were angry because the buses were late – but that wasn't my fault!"

Nina wasn't paid, but she got something better. "At the end of the summer, the manager wrote me a letter about my work. I can show it when I look for a real job." She also made a new friend – a girl from Paris who was staying at the campsite.

Next summer, Nina wants to work at the theatre box office. "I love meeting people," she says. "And I think I'm good at helping them."

items.q: How did Nina hear about the work at the tourist information centre?
options: Someone in her family told her about it.
A friend from school asked her to do it.

items.q: Why did the centre want Nina to help?
options: She knew a lot about the town.
She had worked in an office before.

items.q: What did one man ask Nina to do?
options: find someone to look at his teeth
book a table at a restaurant

items.q: Why did Nina find phone calls difficult?
options: She had to speak French on the phone.
She couldn't see the person she was talking to.
The phone at the centre didn't work well.

items.q: What did Nina get for her work?

part4.title: Public libraries
part4.text:
Libraries have {19} for thousands of years, but the first ones were only for rich people. In the 1800s, many towns in Britain started to {20} public libraries, where anyone could borrow books for free. This was very important, because books were too expensive for most families to buy.

Today libraries do much more than {21} books. Many have computers that you can use, and some also {22} DVDs, music and even games. Lots of libraries organise clubs and events, too. For example, children can {23} part in reading competitions in the summer holidays, and adults can join classes to learn new skills.

Some people think we don't need libraries any more because we can find everything on the internet. But in most towns the library is still a busy place. It's quiet, warm and friendly – and it's a great place to {24} your homework!

items.q: Where are the girl and her dad going first?

script.t: Dad, are we going to the library first? I need to give back my books.
We can't. The library doesn't open until ten on Saturdays.
Oh. What about the post office? You wanted to send Grandma's parcel.
That can wait until later. Let's go to the bank first – I need to get some money.
OK.

items.q: What time is the boy's dentist appointment?

script.t: Don't forget your dentist appointment this afternoon, Tom.
It's at three o'clock, isn't it?
It was, but they phoned this morning and changed it to half past four.
Half past four? But I've got football at the sports centre until four.
That's fine. The dentist is only five minutes from the sports centre.

items.q: Which place did the boy visit on his school trip?

script.t: How was your school trip to London, Ali?
Great! We wanted to see a show at the theatre, but there wasn't one in the afternoon.
Oh no. So what did you do?
We went to the Natural History Museum instead. The dinosaurs were amazing! Some students wanted to go to the cinema after that, but our teacher said there wasn't time.

items.q: Where will the friends meet?

script.t: Shall we meet at the café by the station on Sunday?
It's closed on Sundays. What about outside the Grand Hotel on King Street?
Hmm, I'm not sure where that is. Let's meet at the tourist information centre – it's in the main square.
OK, everyone knows where that is. See you there at ten.

items.q: What is wrong with the family's car?

script.t: Mum, why are we taking the bus today? Where's the car?
It's at the garage. The mechanic is repairing it.
Is it the window again? It wouldn't close last week.
No, Dad fixed that. This time one of the lights at the front is broken.
What about the tyres?
They're fine. The mechanic checked them.

part2.intro: You will hear a radio presenter talking about a new sports centre.
part2.title: Greenfield Sports Centre

items.label: Price of a swim for under-16s: £

script.t: Hello, and welcome to Radio Greenfield. I've got some good news for sports fans today. The new Greenfield Sports Centre is finally ready! We thought it would open this Friday, but the builders needed a little more time, so the big opening day is now Saturday. There'll be free activities all day, so come along. Now, prices. For adults, a swim costs five pounds, but if you're under sixteen, it's only three pounds. That's a great price for such a beautiful pool. And there's lots more to do as well as swimming. There are four tennis courts outside, but the most exciting thing is new for our town – a climbing wall! It's twelve metres high, and there are lessons for beginners every afternoon. After your sport, you can relax in the café on the first floor. It opens at nine in the morning and closes at eight in the evening, so there's lots of time for a drink and a snack. The manager of the sports centre is Mrs Dobson. That's D-O-B-S-O-N. If you have any questions, you can email her through the sports centre website. See you there!

part3.intro: You will hear Lily talking to her friend Sam about her holiday.

items.q: Where was Lily's hotel?
What did Lily like most about the hotel?
What problem did the family have?
How did Lily's family find out about things to do in the town?
What is Lily doing next weekend?
options: going to the cinema with Sam

script.t: Hi Lily! How was your holiday in Italy?
Brilliant, thanks, Sam. We stayed in a hotel for a week.
Was it by the sea? You said you wanted a hotel near the beach.
We did, but all the hotels by the beach were full. So we stayed in the centre of the town. That was OK, because the beach was only ten minutes away by bus.
Was the hotel nice?
Our rooms were quite small, and the food in the restaurant was nothing special. But there was a swimming pool on the roof! That was the best thing. I swam there every morning before breakfast.
Lucky you! Did everything go well? Last year your car broke down, didn't it?

Yes, but not this time! On the first day I thought I'd lost my passport, but it was in Mum's bag. The real problem was my brother. He broke a tooth on a hard sweet, so we had to find a dentist. We spent the whole morning there.
Poor him! How did you know what to do in the town? Did you have a guidebook?

We forgot it at home! And the woman at the hotel reception was always too busy to help. So we went to the tourist information centre. A man there gave us free maps and told us about a great boat trip.
Cool. Hey, do you want to go to the cinema next Saturday? There's a new film on.
I'd love to, but my aunt's bought tickets for all of us to see a musical at the theatre. What about going to the museum on Sunday?
Sorry, I'm visiting my grandma on Sunday. Maybe another time.

items.intro: You will hear a boy phoning a sports centre.
items.q: Why is the boy phoning?
options: to find something he left there

script.t: Hello, is that Riverside Sports Centre?
Yes, how can I help?
I was at the swimming pool yesterday afternoon, and I think I left my blue jacket in the changing room.
Let me look. Yes, someone gave us a blue jacket. Is your name inside it?
Yes, it's Tom Kerr. Can I come and get it after school?
Of course. We're open until nine.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking to a friend about a new café.
items.q: What does she like most about the café?

script.t: Have you been to the new café on Bridge Street?
Not yet. Is it good?

Yes! It isn't cheap – a hot chocolate costs four pounds. And they play music all the time, which I don't really like. But the people who work there are so friendly. The waiter remembered my name the second time I went!

items.intro: You will hear a man talking to a travel agent.
items.q: What does the man want to change?

script.t: Good morning. Last week I booked a holiday in Spain here for my family.
Yes, I remember. Four people, flying on the twelfth of August.
That's right. The date's fine, and there are still four of us. But we've looked at the hotel on the internet, and it's a long way from the beach. Could you find us a different one?
Of course. Let me have a look.

items.intro: You will hear a girl talking about a visit to the theatre.
items.q: How did she feel about the play?
options: It was too long for her.
She enjoyed it more than she expected.
She found the language too difficult.

script.t: Our class went to the theatre in the city last night to see a play by Shakespeare. I thought it would be boring, because the language is so old and difficult. But the actors were fantastic and really funny, and I understood almost everything! I didn't want it to finish. I'm going to ask my parents to take me again.

items.intro: You will hear a librarian talking to some students.
items.q: Why is the librarian talking to the students?
options: to tell them about new opening times
to give them the results of a competition
to ask them to join the library

script.t: Good morning, everyone. I'm Mrs Patel from the town library. I'm here today because our opening times are changing. From next Monday, we'll open at eight o'clock, not half past nine, so you can come in before school. And on Saturdays we'll stay open until five. Oh, and the results of our story competition will be on our website next month. Thank you.

part5.intro: You will hear Oliver talking to his mum about Saturday. Where is each person going?

script.t: Oliver, it's going to be a busy Saturday tomorrow. Everyone's going somewhere different.
Is Dad taking me to football?
No, sorry. Dad has to take the car to the garage first thing in the morning. The brakes are making a strange noise.
Oh. What about Grandma? Can she take me?
Grandma's busy too. She wanted to go to the bank, but she can do that on Monday. Tomorrow she's going to the hairdresser's. She's having her hair cut for Aunt Sue's wedding.
And Kate? Is she going to the library again? She's always there.
Not this time. She has to see the dentist at ten. Her tooth is still hurting.
Poor Kate. Is Uncle Jim coming to visit us?
No, he's going into town. He wanted to send some letters at the post office, but I said I'd do that for him. He's going to the travel agent to book his holiday to Canada.
So how do I get to my football match at the sports centre?
You can ride your bike. It's only ten minutes away.
OK. I'll leave at nine, then.
